summary: Shell research program phase 6 after a dive wave: one opus agent harvests the new consolidations, appends the landing report to the topic map, applies the stop condition, and commissions the next wave (revised staged briefs plus follow-ups) or declares ready-to-draft with binding authoring notes
logs: Verdict: needs-another-round · next wave 8 · IDs 371 · MUST 251 · families 21 · contradictions 30

harvest.verdict_reason: Wave 3 added 172 IDs and 127 MUST rules (371 IDs, 251 MUST, 21 families). Of those MUST rules, 94 sit in the nine families opened this wave (SH-ZSH, SH-FISH, SH-NU, SH-ELV, SH-INST, PS-SEC, SH-SEC, SH-TEST, SH-CORE). The wave also found new failure classes, for example the zsh emulate errexit reset, the fish || skip, the nu tail-try hang, cargo-dist failing open, sudo-rs -E, bats and Pester vacuous exits, and the zizmor dotted-matrix miss. No out-of-corpus held-out round has run: the security 'held-out' round resampled the corpus's own 40 clones (shell-security.md:13) and still found a missing class. Load-bearing questions answerable by fixture runs remain: the held-out round, completeness of the SH-SEC-02 check, and the ble.sh and Windows clauses of the SH-EMIT-24/43 MUST rules. The next wave is the held-out round plus two small revisions. If that round is clean (only instances of existing classes and check fixes), the next iterate returns ready-to-draft.

next_wave.label: Revision: variable-carried secrets, credential forms, names outside bash
next_wave.brief:
Revision of shell-security.md. IDs SH-SEC-01..12 stay stable; any new rule takes SH-SEC-13 or above.
Three questions, each load-bearing:
(1) Completeness of SH-SEC-02's check. A secret that reaches argv through a variable is invisible to s02-argv. Examples: h="Authorization: Bearer $T"; curl -H "$h"; args+=(-H "...$T"); a URL with userinfo built in a variable. Write checks/secret-argv.sh as a two-pass awk script: pass 1 marks variables assigned from secret-named sources, pass 2 flags their use in curl, wget, git, docker, gh or cargo argv. It follows the SH-GATE-30/31 shape: awk only, exit map 0/1/69/74/78/79. Watch it red on plants and green on twins on GNU, busybox 1.37 and uutils (SH-GATE-33 hosts). Measure precision on the 40 corpus clones (SS/mine-argv.sh baseline), on the fleet, and on heldout/shell trees if present (do not wait for them). Decide: MUST cell or listing cell.
(2) Credential remedy forms the rule recommends but never ran (security Q1). Cover git through GIT_ASKPASS, credential.helper store/cache and an http.extraHeader passed through the environment, against userinfo URLs, checking .git/config persistence and /proc/<pid>/cmdline. Cover cargo login reading the token on stdin and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN in the environment, against a stub alternative registry. Run each on the matrix and record what argv shows.
(3) The scope of SH-SEC-09 outside bash. Run local "$k=v", typeset -n, read "$k" and printf-style dynamic names on dash, busybox ash, mksh, ksh93u+m, yash, posh and zsh, via matrix.sh posix and zsh.
Fixtures go under shell-tools/fixtures/shell-security-rev/. Decide amendments by ID, and log them in a Revision log section.
